findings.passage: SB14 will require Texas voters to display a current government-issued photo ID to cast a ballot.
findings.note: Op-ed by West on the Senate site about SB 14 (2011). He goes on to say no evidence supports the claim of fake registration cards at polls and that SB 14 does not address mail-in ballot improprieties.

findings.passage: Evidence does exist that minorities, the elderly and disabled are more likely to be without a driver license or state-issued photo ID.
findings.note: Op-ed by West on SB 14 (2011), on who lacks photo ID.
subjects: what happens to a voter with no ID

findings.passage: Democrats support laws that insure the integrity of the ballot. But SB14 does not address known improprieties surrounding mail-in ballots.
findings.note: Op-ed by West on SB 14 (2011), on mail ballots versus polling-place ID.

findings.passage: We argued that poor people and minorities would be made to pay for the right to vote - a de facto poll tax.
findings.note: News release after the US Justice Department refused to clear SB 14; West describes the objections he and other opponents made in 2011. The release also says voters could keep using their voter registration cards as the main ID.

findings.passage: Last week's ruling by the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals marks a victory for many like myself who have said since 2011, that the Voter ID law passed by the Texas Legislature that year was discriminatory.
findings.note: Op-ed by West on the 2015 Fifth Circuit ruling on SB 14. He also says a possible fix is adding more accepted ID types, such as a student photo ID.

findings.passage: Voter ID supporters claim the law was put in place to fight voter fraud. But the rampant fraud they claim has never been documented.
findings.note: Statement by West on the Fifth Circuit's 2016 ruling on SB 14.

findings.passage: Is SB 16 truly protecting our elections, or is it creating new barriers to the ballot box?
findings.note: West's Austin Report e-newsletter on SB 16, the proof-of-citizenship bill. The PDF text layer has scan errors; the sentence is cleaned of them. He goes on to describe the required documents and the limited federal ballot.

findings.passage: Requiring individuals to present proof of citizenship may do more harm than good, introducing errors and unnecessary barriers into the voting process.
findings.note: West's Austin Report e-newsletter on SB 16. Text layer has scan errors; the sentence is cleaned of them. He also says non-citizen voting is already illegal under state and federal law.

findings.passage: The Texas Attorney General's website says that since 2005, the office has successfully prosecuted 534 offenses related to election fraud involving 155 persons.
findings.note: News release on SB 7 and its special-session successor, about claims of widespread voter fraud. He also objects to the planned county voter-roll monitoring by the Secretary of State.

findings.passage: "It is imperative that we have an honest discussion as it relates to the intent of the 2nd Amendment, now within the context of military-styled assault rifles that are in the hands of civilians; and too many times in the hands of those who should not have them," said Senator West.
findings.note: Senate press release after the Uvalde shooting, on his appointment to the Senate special committee. He calls for a discussion of the Second Amendment and military-style rifles held by civilians.

findings.passage: "Other areas that should be explored include mandatory cooling-off periods before the completion of certain firearms purchases and the fact that the majority of Texans and Americans support universal background checks.
findings.note: Same release. He lists waiting periods and universal background checks as topics for the committee to examine.

findings.passage: Senator West, formerly a Chief Felony Prosecutor for Dallas County, authored a bill to ban assault weapons during his first Legislative Session in 1993. He has been an advocate for common-sense gun regulations for nearly 30 years, writing and supporting bills that require trigger locks, would close gun show loopholes and prohibit straw purchases of guns for people who cannot legally buy them.
findings.note: Background paragraph in a release issued by his office (third person). It says he authored an assault weapons ban bill in 1993 and wrote or supported bills on trigger locks, gun show sales and straw purchases. No bill numbers given.

findings.passage: In grappling with the impact of gun violence, I've experienced a gamut of emotions. Yes, I support 2nd Amendment rights, but I'm saddened by the continued, senseless loss of lives.
findings.note: Op-ed by West posted on the Senate press room. He states support for Second Amendment rights while calling for gun-violence measures.

findings.passage: Following the fatal shooting at Santa Fe High, (Texas) in 2018, special Senate and House committees on School Safety were formed leading up to the 2019 Legislative Session. Governor Greg Abbott toured the state to highlight his report and recommendations; among them, a "red flag" law that would temporarily suspend the ability of potentially dangerous individuals to possess or purchase firearms.
findings.note: In his op-ed he describes the 2019 red-flag proposal; the passage describes it and does not itself state his view of it.

findings.passage: Personally, I don't feel safer knowing that neither a license or training is required to publicly carry a firearm in the state where I and my family live.
findings.note: Statement the day after the Uvalde shooting, on Texas carrying without a license or training.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.passage: "Let's not underscore the importance of what we're doing, as relates to some of these issues, more specifically, the issue concerning firearms, that's the big issue right there, and how people in the state of Texas want to deal with that."
findings.note: CBS Texas quotes West after his appointment to the Senate special committee; he calls firearms the big issue for the committee.

findings.passage: "We've got to look at our mental health system again... And we've got to look at the issue concerning weapons in the state of Texas."
findings.note: FOX 7 Austin quotes West on the committee's work; date from the page's publish stamp.
